origin.description: Regress the first difference on the lagged level, and on lagged differences when lags is positive.
origin.usage: ur.df(y, type = c("none", "drift", "trend"), lags = 1, selectlags = c("Fixed", "AIC", "BIC"))

arguments.name: y
arguments.text: A numeric series. A matrix with more than one column is rejected, and a missing value is rejected.

arguments.name: type
arguments.text: none omits the intercept. drift adds it. trend adds the intercept and a time index.

arguments.name: lags
arguments.text: How many lagged differences to include. The regression embed is one wider than this number.

arguments.name: selectlags
arguments.text: Fixed keeps every requested lag. AIC and BIC drop lags by the usual penalty, counting the variance as a parameter.

origin.details: The stored lag is the requested integer. The regression uses that integer plus one as the embed width, so a request of 1 places one lagged difference next to the lagged level. The critical-value row is chosen from the length of the first difference.
origin.value: The t ratio of the lagged level, and the nested F ratios when an intercept or a trend is present, with the Dickey-Fuller critical-value rows.
